questions.question: Who should be the merchant of record when hotels on the platform collect guest payments? (Your brief says selling the software does not automatically make Monoclay the merchant.)

options.label: Hotel is merchant, Stripe Connect (Recommended)
options.description: Each hotel's legal entity has its own connected payment account and is merchant of record. Monoclay is the platform and can take a platform fee. Fastest to build and keeps card data out of our systems. Adyen or other providers can be added later behind the same interface.

options.label: Hotels bring their own processor
options.description: Hotels connect a gateway they already have (Adyen, Stripe, local banks). Monoclay earns nothing on payments, and we need more adapters.

options.label: Monoclay as payment facilitator
options.description: Monoclay onboards merchants and earns a payment margin, like Mews Payments and Cloudbeds Payments. Requires payment-facilitator registration, merchant identity checks (KYC), risk management and much heavier compliance.

questions.question: Which country or region should the first pilot be built for? This sets which taxes, fiscal rules, currency, languages and data residency come first. Other regions follow later.

options.label: Maldives / Indian Ocean
options.description: Island resorts with seaplane and boat transfers, TGST, Green Tax per guest-night, service charge, and USD/MVR.

options.label: GCC (UAE / Saudi)
options.description: VAT, municipality and tourism fees, ZATCA e-invoicing in Saudi Arabia, Arabic right-to-left UI.

options.label: EU / UK
options.description: VAT, GDPR, card authentication rules (SCA/3DS2) and country fiscalization (Germany TSE, Italy, Portugal, etc.).

options.label: United States
options.description: State and city occupancy taxes, FTC resort-fee disclosure rule, USD only.

questions.question: Which property type should the first pilot be? Every type stays in scope. This only sets build order and the first end-to-end demo.

options.label: Independent / boutique hotel
options.description: Fastest path to a live pilot. Core reservations, front desk, housekeeping, folios, night audit and a booking engine, with no resort extras at first.

options.label: Resort
options.description: Villas, meal plans and allowances, transfers, activities, spa and outlets linked to the stay. Heavier, but this is where the strongest differentiation is.

options.label: Hotel group / multi-property
options.description: Portfolio policies, cross-property guest profiles and consolidated reporting from the start.

options.label: Serviced apartments
options.description: Long stays, unit-based inventory, owner accounting and automated communication.

questions.question: Which tech stack should the platform use?

options.label: TypeScript end-to-end (Recommended)
options.description: Node.js backend, React web apps, mobile as an offline-capable web app (React Native later), PostgreSQL. One language across API, web and mobile, the largest hiring pool, and the fastest to build with AI assistance.

options.label: Kotlin/JVM backend + TS frontend
options.description: Spring/Kotlin backend in the style of banking systems. Very strong typing for finance, but slower to iterate and two languages for the team.

options.label: Go backend + TS frontend
options.description: Fast, simple services with a small runtime. Less expressive for complex domain logic.

options.label: .NET (C#) backend + TS frontend
options.description: Strong for enterprise and Microsoft-heavy hotel groups. Two languages for the team.

questions.question: Which cloud should the platform run on? I'll define all infrastructure as code (Terraform) and run everything locally and in CI until you provide cloud credentials.

options.label: AWS (Recommended)
options.description: The broadest managed services and what hotel-group IT and security reviewers usually expect. Regions near the Maldives: Mumbai, UAE and Singapore.

options.label: Google Cloud
options.description: Strong managed Kubernetes and data/analytics tools. Regions in Mumbai, Delhi, Doha and Singapore.

options.label: Azure
options.description: Good fit for hotel groups that run on Microsoft. Regions in the UAE and India.

options.label: Cloud-agnostic Kubernetes
options.description: Portable across clouds, but more operational work and less use of managed services.

questions.question: This session can't create GitHub repositories itself. What should the main repository be called? You'll create it empty and private at github.com/monoclay-studio, and I'll attach it and push. Until then I work locally, so nothing is blocked.

options.label: monoclay (Recommended)
options.description: One private monorepo for the whole platform: services, web apps, mobile, SDKs, infrastructure, docs.

options.label: monoclay-platform
options.description: Same monorepo with a more explicit name.

options.label: monoclay-pms
options.description: Named after the core product.

questions.question: How should real OTA connections (Booking.com, Expedia, Airbnb, Agoda) start? Either way I build our own channel-manager core plus an OTA simulator for testing. This decides which real path you pursue commercially.

options.label: Connectivity hub first (Recommended)
options.description: Plug into a white-label channel API (e.g. Channex) for quick access to hundreds of channels, with a per-property cost. Apply for direct certifications later.

options.label: Direct certifications first
options.description: You apply now to the Booking.com and Expedia connectivity partner programs. No hub fees, but months of certification before going live.

options.label: Both in parallel
options.description: Use a hub to launch and pursue direct certifications at the same time.

questions.question: Is there a pilot property, and what system does it run today? This decides which migration importer I build first (all of them are planned).

options.label: Yes, runs OPERA / Fidelio
options.description: Prioritise the OPERA importer, which handles profiles, future reservations, deposits, AR and rate codes.

options.label: Yes, on another cloud PMS
options.description: For example Cloudbeds, Mews, eZee or RoomRaccoon. Prioritise CSV and API importers.

options.label: No pilot yet
options.description: Build with realistic Maldives sample data: a guesthouse, a 120-villa resort and a 3-property group.
